item.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.
item.dc:creator: Sebastiano Cominelli, R\'egis Cottereau, Sergey Gavrilyuk, Bruno Lombard, Fabien Petitpas

item.title: Quasideterminants and differential realizations of W-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.31794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular $W$-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of $\mathfrak{gl}_{np}$. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of $n$ evaluation differential realizations of $\mathfrak{gl}_p$. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Derkachov, Daniil Getta

item.title: Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.
item.dc:creator: Haoyi Li

item.title: Averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over $U(N)$, with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, $N$. We also calculate the so-called zero-swap and one-swap contributions to an average with any number of traces, which amounts to determining general trace moments in a range double the size of the renowned result of Diaconis and Shahshahani. The expression is tractable enough to use in applications, for example to determine the parameter range where certain trace averages assume negative values.
item.dc:creator: Ada Bendel, Rhys Cahill, John Brian Conrey, Gregor Harrison Barraclough, Ayesha Irfan, Nina Claire Snaith, Leonid Tyulenev

item.title: On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.
item.dc:creator: Ayesha Irfan

item.title: The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns
item.description: arXiv:2610.32618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the free energy of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $\alpha$ and temperature $T$, and we give it as an explicit variational principle. The Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation maps the model onto $N$ Ising spins coupled to $M=\alpha N$ Gaussian hidden units, whose radius, the empirical variance of the hidden layer, is a thermodynamic variable with an entropic cost. At fixed radius the model is an Ising--spherical spin glass with Gaussian couplings, which we solve. The principle (i) reproduces the Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky theory as its replica-symmetric restriction, (ii) identifies $T_g=1+\sqrt\alpha$ as the rigorous boundary of the annealed region, (iii) selects a unique spin-glass solution of the AGS equations, and (iv) gives the radius an equation of state. Moreover, (v) below $T_g$ we prove that replica symmetry is broken throughout: the instability of the AGS solution reduces to the zero-field de Almeida-Thouless condition of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Camilli, Pierluigi Contucci, Emanuele Mingione

item.title: Correlation-induced suppression of Granger causality and Gaussian transfer entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.32867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In complex dynamical systems, Granger causality and transfer entropy are widely used to infer directional interactions, but they quantify a source's unique predictive contribution after conditioning and can therefore be substantially attenuated by correlation with the retained variables. Here, using our previously developed Linear Operator Causality Analysis (LOCA) framework, which measures causal response from the system propagator, we derive a relationship between predictive and operator-based causality. For a two-dimensional linear system, the fractional suppression of Granger causality equals the squared correlation between source and receiver. We generalize this result to high-dimensional systems using the source covariance remaining after conditioning and show that additional conditioning can only increase the suppression. The same covariance ordering yields a corresponding upper bound for Gaussian transfer entropy. A linearized Burgers advection chain exhibits 36.6% suppression at the convective travel-time peak, and exact nonlinear acoustic Burgers solutions show that the fitted-surrogate penalty is governed by correlation structure rather than nonlinearity and remains robust to sensor noise after operator debiasing. Applied to resting-state fMRI from the Human Connectome Project (80 brain regions, 8 functional networks, 10 subjects), the single-lag Granger causality measure falls 39.4% below the operator response when conditioning only on the receiver and 73.0% when conditioning on the receiver and all other retained variables. The framework provides a quantitative bridge between predictive and operator-based causal measures in high-dimensional dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Louis Cattafesta, Scott T. M. Dawson, Ankit Srivastava

item.title: Variance of relative entropy over random states
item.description: arXiv:2610.32899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Average relative entropy over major generic random states is recently studied. In this work, the investigation is extended by deriving the variances of relative entropy over the Hilbert--Schmidt and Bures--Hall ensembles, which characterize its fluctuations around the average value. Exact results for the variances of relative entropy between independent states drawn from the same ensemble and from two different ensembles are obtained. These results further indicate that the average relative entropy is typical in the considered limiting regimes. In addition to the matrix-level calculations similar to the average relative entropy, eigenvalue correlation functions of the ensembles are involved in the variance computations through the use of zonal polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Linfeng Wei, Lu Wei

item.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.32973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincar\'e variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincar\'e method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Gay-Balmaz, Tudor S. Ratiu, Cesare Tronci

item.title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
item.description: arXiv:2610.30466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.
item.dc:creator: Achilleas V. Koukas, Mariem Magdy, Juan A. Valiente Kroon

item.title: M5-brane source charges, Chern--Connes pairings and noncommutative compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.31674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate a source-adapted Chern--Connes description of M5-brane magnetic charge in physically motivated noncommutative and quotient linking sectors. The starting point is the local codimension-five geometry of an M5-brane source: the magnetic charge is measured on a four-dimensional link. In the smooth local model the link is the ordinary four-sphere, and the pairing reduces to the standard flux integral of the M-theory four-form field strength. The construction is motivated by the published even-codimensional Noncommutative Foliation Invariant (NCFI for short), where Connes' transverse fundamental cyclic cocycle is paired with an even transverse-geometric \(K\)-class. For an M5-brane the relevant codimension is odd, so the required odd \(K\)-class is supplied instead by the boundary map of the source/linking extension. Noncommutative or groupoid algebras are used only when they arise from physical mechanisms: Matrix/M-theory compactification on noncommutative tori, reduction to D-branes in background \(B\)-fields, large \(C\)-field M5 limits, or quotient/orbifold source links. The result is a topological charge formula, not a derivation of the full M5-brane dynamics or of the complete M-theory action.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis P. Zois

item.title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal. The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.
item.dc:creator: Hang Du, Shuyang Gong, Brice Huang, Zhangsong Li

item.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31865v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.
item.dc:creator: Hac\`{e}ne Belbachir, Jos\'{e} Ricardo G. Mendon\c{c}a

item.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
item.description: arXiv:2610.31872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.
item.dc:creator: M. Fenucci

item.title: Probabilistic representation and Monte Carlo method for nonlinear Dirac equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dirac equations describe the relativistic evolution of quantum particles. Using the point-process stochastic calculus of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) on general state spaces, which naturally allows additional Feynman-Kac potentials, we develop a probabilistic representation for the nonlinear Dirac equations in $1+1$ spacetime dimension with cubic nonlinearity and $L_\infty$-type problem data using a multi-type branching telegraph process together with both continuous and jump-type multiplicative functionals. Our main theorem leads to a classification result which, when applied to the specific Soler model, gives a sharp finite-time admissibility of the probabilistic representation. By extending the one-step representation to a multi-step, time-marching representation using an analytically-derived a priori $L_\infty$ estimate, we observe a ``local probabilistic representation, but global PDE well-posedness" phenomenon. We proceed to propose a time-marching Monte Carlo algorithm as a global numerical solver for the Soler system with a rigorous convergence proof and establish an additional stability result on the PDE side. Finally, while the underlying process parameters do not affect the validity of the probabilistic representation, we observe their potential for variance reduction in the Monte Carlo methods.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Fouque, Tomoyuki Ichiba, Ka Lok Lam

item.title: Can Spontaneous Time-Translation Symmetry Breaking Be Quantized Without Explicit Branches?
item.description: arXiv:2610.32030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can classically branched dynamics associated with spontaneous time-translation-symmetry breaking be quantized without explicitly retaining the branches of the Hamiltonian? We investigate this question using a reduced phase space. formulation in which the Hamiltonian is single-valued, while the critical structure of the classical Legendre map is encoded in a singular, momentum-dependent symplectic geometry. Quantization of the reduced Poisson algebra yields a deformed position-momentum commutator whose singularities determine distinct regular momentum sectors. Using the positive measure induced by the reduced symplectic structure, we identify a bounded central sector and two unbounded outer sectors. In the central sector, states with vanishing mean momentum obey a nonzero lower bound on position uncertainty, subject to the operator-domain assumptions of the representation. We further identify a possible field-theoretic connection with k-essence, where nonlinear scalar-field kinetics can produce finite-velocity degeneracies of the Legendre map. The relationship between the resulting reduced quantum description and branch-matching quantization remains unresolved and requires a comparison of the corresponding Hilbert spaces and operator domains.
item.dc:creator: Partha Nandi

item.title: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
item.description: arXiv:2610.32227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.
item.dc:creator: Sakibul Islam Rayhan, Karima Hassan, Md Rasedujjaman, Md Mohsinur Rahman Adnan

item.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
item.description: arXiv:2610.32291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers $b,s\ge2$. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever \[ \frac{b}{\sqrt{s}} \left( \frac{b\sqrt{s(s-1)}}{bs-1} \right)^{s-1}<1. \] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices ($d=3$, or equivalently $s=b^2$), regardless of the choice of $b$. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. In the intermediate regime $1+\log17/\log6\le d<3$, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on $b$ and $s$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.
item.dc:creator: Manaka Okuyama, Masayuki Ohzeki

item.title: Commuting Families of Flag Quasideterminants in Reflection Equation Algebras of Type A
item.description: arXiv:2610.32521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a family of northeastern antidiagonal quasideterminants associated with the successive blocks of the generating matrix of a reflection equation (RE) algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. Our main result proves the conjecture on their pairwise commutativity formulated earlier. The proof uses the triangular realization of the RE algebra in a quantum enveloping algebra and the flag property of quasideterminants. We also discuss the interpretation of these elements in terms of quantum cluster coordinates and their possible connection with generalized Toda systems.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry V. Talalaev

item.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.32600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).
item.dc:creator: Filip Ficek, Maciej Maliborski

item.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
item.description: arXiv:2610.32649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
item.dc:creator: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.32659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.
item.dc:creator: Peter T. J. Bradshaw, Jonte R. Hance

item.title: Avalanches of the Abelian sandpile on the hierarchical lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.32687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Abelian sandpile model on a sequence of finite fractal graphs: the hierarchical, or Migdal--Kadanoff, lattices. Our first main result consists of matching power-law tail bounds for the avalanche and the uniform wave started at certain "pivotal" vertices. We also establish a limiting result for the pivotal reach of the avalanche and, finally, a scaling limit for the size of a uniform wave started at a vertex of high degree.
item.dc:creator: Luca Cattani, Leandro Chiarini, Alessandra Cipriani

item.title: Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.32701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.
item.dc:creator: Panagiota Birmpa, Patr\'icia Gon\c{c}alves, Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis

item.title: Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.32710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.
item.dc:creator: Federico Finkel, Artemio Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Mart\'in Zapata

item.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
item.dc:creator: Dean Wang

item.title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.32751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Yangshanshan Liu

item.title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.32769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=\varphi(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(\varphi,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a M\"obius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.
item.dc:creator: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota

item.title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
item.description: arXiv:2610.32821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=\pi^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai, Xinyi Li, Daisuke Shiraishi, Aoteng Xia

item.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.32829v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.
item.dc:creator: Lo\"is Delande (AGM - UMR 8088), Tony Leli\`evre (CERMICS), Boris Nectoux (LMBP), Thomas Normand

item.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The scaling limits of interfaces in the critical two-dimensional Ising model are described by the Schramm--Loewner evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. While, in the scaling limit, the law of the whole near-critical FK-Ising configuration is known to be singular with respect to the critical law in the thermal direction, and the same is expected for the spin configuration, we prove in this paper that the law of a single interface is not. More precisely, we consider the Ising model with mesh $\delta$ in the Dobrushin square at $\beta=\beta_c-m\delta$, where $m\ne0$ is fixed, and we prove that the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of the interface with respect to its critical law has moments of every positive and negative order, bounded uniformly in $\delta$, so that the law of every subsequential scaling limit of the interface is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to that of $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. Our analysis explains the mechanism behind this result: the logarithmically growing specific heat (that is, the variance of the Hamiltonian, normalized by the number of edges) cancels between the full domain and the domain slit along the interface.
item.dc:creator: Yu Feng

item.title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
item.description: arXiv:2610.32927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a probabilistic approach to the ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model. The model is formally described by the density $\exp(\alpha\int \mathopen{:} \cos(\beta X) \mathclose{:} )$, where $X$ is a log-correlated Gaussian field. Our construction applies on bounded convex domains for every particle activity $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and throughout the subcritical range $\beta^2\in[0,4)$, below the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless threshold. We apply the martingale method introduced by Lacoin, Rhodes and Vargas to two dimensions by using refined estimates based on charge conjugation symmetries. Our result extends existing constructions by treating the full subcritical regime for a broad class of covariances.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Bonnefont, Hermanni Rajam\"aki, Vincent Vargas

item.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.18791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.
item.dc:creator: David Keating, Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model: relation to Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat and 1-site classical XYZ model with boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2601.06826v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a description of the classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 8 independent coupling constants through a pair of ${\rm BC}_1$ type classical Sklyanin algebras generated by the (classical) quadratic reflection equation with non-dynamical XYZ $r$-matrix. For this purpose, we consider the classical version of the $L$-operator for the Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model proposed by O. Chalykh. In ${\rm BC}_1$ case it is factorized to the product of two Lax matrices depending on 4 constants. Then we apply an IRF-Vertex type gauge transformation and obtain a product of the Lax matrices for the Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostats. Each of them is described by the ${\rm BC}_1$ version of the classical Sklyanin algebra. In particular case, when 4 pairs of constants coincide, the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model exactly coincides with the relativistic Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat. Explicit change of variables is obtained. We also consider another special case of the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 7 independent constants. We show that it can be reproduced by considering the transfer matrix of the classical 1-site XYZ chain with boundaries. In the end of the paper, using another gauge transformation we represent the Chalykh's Lax matrix in a form depending on the Sklyanin's generators.
item.dc:creator: A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov

item.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
item.description: arXiv:2607.17002v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Master--slave synchronization reconstructs the evolving state of a reference (or master) system by continuously correcting a second system, the slave, using observations of the master. In applications, the observations are often contaminated by noise, so the corrections injected into the slave are themselves uncertain. In this paper we aim at quantifying the effect of noisy observations on master--slave synchronization for a family of evolution equations that combine a quadratic transport term with a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin and Nikolaevskiy equations, among others. Under periodic boundary conditions, a Fourier--Galerkin approximation of order $K$ yields a finite-dimensional master--slave system in which white observation noise of intensity $\sigma$ is modeled through an It\^o stochastic differential equation. In this framework, we first establish local exponential stability of noiseless synchronization for sufficiently strong scalar coupling. Then we compare the stochastic synchronization error with its noiseless counterpart resulting from the same initial slave state, isolating in this way the effect of noise. Assuming bounded reference paths, the mean-square deviation between the noiseless and noisy synchronization errors is $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ on finite time intervals. Under additional regularity assumptions, we also bound the error between the finite-resolution stochastic slave model and the infinite-dimensional deterministic master field, explicitly separating spectral approximation error, deterministic synchronization error and observation noise. Numerical experiments for the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations confirm the predicted noise scaling.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Miguez, In\'es P. Mari\~no

item.title: The para--Krawtchouk oscillator and its continuum limit
item.description: arXiv:2609.30619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The para-Krawtchouk polynomials define, through their recurrence relation, a finite oscillator model that exhibits fractional revival. We determine the continuum limit of this Hamiltonian, both from its recurrence relation and directly on the polynomials. The limit is the singular (isotonic) oscillator $-\partial_\eta^2+\eta^2+\tfrac{\gamma^2-1}{4\eta^2}$. The deformation parameter $\gamma$ survives as a central impurity of the couplings, which decays as the inverse square of the distance. This is the marginal rate, which the continuum scaling turns into a finite $\sfrac{1}{\eta^2}$ term. Using the decomposition of the para-Krawtchouk polynomials into two Hahn families, we prove the confluence, for every degree, of the eigenvectors on the two sub-lattices to generalized Hermite functions. The bispectral pair of the discrete model, which generates the Hahn algebra, becomes in the limit a pair of generators of $\su$, the dynamical algebra of the singular oscillator.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Z. Beaulac, Nicolas Cramp\'e, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Marlon Josue Rivera Valladares, Luc Vinet

item.title: Para families of orthogonal polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.38211v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The para-Krawtchouk polynomials arose in the search for spin chains with perfect state transfer; the para-Racah, $q$-para-Racah and para-Bannai--Ito polynomials followed, obtained through singular truncations of families of the Askey scheme and used in turn to design spin chains. All are orthogonal on bi-lattices; the prefix goes back to the para-Krawtchouk case, whose spectrum is that of the parabose oscillator. The representations that these polynomials provide of the corresponding algebras --- Hahn, Racah, $q$-Racah, Bannai--Ito and complementary Bannai--Ito --- are shown to be reducible. Each decomposes into a direct sum of two irreducible modules of the same algebra, one attached to each of the two interlaced sub-lattices, and the parameters of the submodules are given. The para polynomials are thereby expressed in terms of the classical polynomials that the submodules carry, and the pairing $\lambda_n=\lambda_{N-n}$ of their eigenvalues is accounted for; the three features of the bi-lattice setting on which the reduction rests are identified. The properties of the para families are then presented in a unified way in the light of this decomposition, together with the constructions through which these families arise and the settings in which they have been put to use.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Z. Beaulac, Nicolas Cramp\'e, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Rafael I. Nepomechie, Luc Vinet

item.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr Gamayun

item.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2610.28497v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Anton Selemenchuk

item.title: Singularity of the spectrum of typical minimal smooth area-preserving flows in any genus
item.description: arXiv:2505.13193v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces, and show that almost every such locally Hamiltonian flow with only simple saddles has singular spectrum. Furthermore, we prove that for almost every pair of such flows, the elements of the pair are spectrally disjoint. More generally, the results from which these statements are deduced are singularity of the spectrum and pairwise spectral disjointness for special flows over full measure sets of interval exchange transformations under a roof with symmetric logarithmic singularities. Spectral singularity is proved using a criterion based on tightness of Birkhoff sums with exponential tail decay. The assumptions of the criterion are verified exploiting the cancellations proved by the last author to prove the absence of mixing in this class of flows, by showing that the latter can be combined with rigidity by exploiting the local product structure of Rauzy-Veech induction. Pairwise spectral disjointness then follows by producing mixing times (for the second flow), using a new mechanism for shearing based on what we call resonant rigidity times.
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Fr\k{a}czek, Adam Kanigowski, Corinna Ulcigrai

item.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2509.25553v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Amp\`ere equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.
item.dc:creator: Maria Deliyianni, Shankar C. Venkataramani

item.title: Testing Transformer Learnability on the Arithmetic Sequence of Rooted Trees
item.description: arXiv:2512.01870v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether a transformer network can learn the deterministic sequence of trees generated by the iterated prime factorization of the natural numbers. Each integer is mapped into a rooted planar tree and the resulting sequence $\mathbb{N}\mathscr{T}$ defines an arithmetic text with measurable statistical structure. A transformer network (the GPT-2 architecture) is trained from scratch on the first $10^{11}$ elements and evaluated on next-token prediction and masked-token prediction tasks, with a Hidden Markov Model as baseline and a scaling analysis over context window, dataset size, vocabulary size and model size. The model reaches a word accuracy of about $0.4$, well above the baseline, and its performance remains stable on test blocks located at $10^{13}$-$10^{15}$, far beyond the training interval. Moreover, the likelihood assigned by the trained model separates the arithmetic text from two controls: synthetic token sequences that preserve the marginal token frequencies but not their order, with a separation that widens with the context, and sequences containing more than three consecutive square-free integers, a configuration that arithmetic forbids. These results indicate that the transformer captures regularities of the arithmetic text that go beyond its frequency profile.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Breccia, Federica Gerace, Marco Lippi, Gabriele Sicuro, Pierluigi Contucci

item.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2602.03441v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via \v{C}ech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.
item.dc:creator: Severin Bunk, Lukas M\"uller, Joost Nuiten, Richard J. Szabo

item.title: Optimal Universal Bounds for Quantum Divergences
item.description: arXiv:2603.09885v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify a universal structural principle underlying the smoothing of classical divergences: the optimizer of the smoothing problem is a clipped probability vector, independently of the specific divergence. This yields a divergence-independent characterization of all smoothed classical divergences and reveals a common geometric structure behind seemingly different quantities. Building on this structural insight, we derive optimal universal bounds for smoothed quantum divergences, including quantum R\'enyi divergences of arbitrary order and the hypothesis-testing divergence. Our inequalities relate divergences of different orders through bounds of the form $D_\beta^{\varepsilon} \le D_\alpha + \mathrm{correction}$ and $D_\beta^{\varepsilon} \ge D_\alpha + \mathrm{correction}$, and we prove that the correction terms are optimal among all universal, state-independent inequalities of this type. Consequently, our results strictly improve previously known bounds whenever those were suboptimal, and in cases where earlier bounds coincide with ours, our analysis establishes their optimality. In particular, we obtain optimal universal bounds for the hypothesis-testing divergence.
item.dc:creator: Gilad Gour

item.title: Correctness of Biot's model of in situ leaching for incompressible liquid and compressible solid components
item.description: arXiv:2604.22645v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a mathematical model of in situ leaching of rare metals, in which the joint filtration of two liquids is governed by the microscopic model $\mathbb{A}^{\varepsilon}$. A key difficulty is the unknown (free) boundary $\Gamma(r)$ between solid and liquid components, determined by an additional condition on $\Gamma(r)$; no standard methods exist for this nonlinear problem. To resolve it, we apply the fixed point theorem. For a given function $r(\boldsymbol{x},t)$ from a set $\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$ of sufficiently smooth functions describing the skeleton structure, we consider the auxiliary problem $\mathbb{B}^{\varepsilon}(r)$: an elliptic system for displacements of the liquid and solid components coupled with parabolic equations for the acid concentration. Selecting the weak solution of minimal smoothness, we apply the homogenization method to pass from the microscopic to the macroscopic description. The resulting macroscopic model $\mathbb{H}(r)$ contains a homogenized boundary condition that expresses the normal boundary velocity $V_{N}=\partial r/\partial t$ as a linear function of the acid concentration $c$. Since $c$ depends on $r$ via an operator $\mathbb{F}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}\to\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$, we prove that $\mathbb{F}$ is Lipschitz continuous and, by Banach's theorem, possesses a unique fixed point $r^{*}$, which yields the unique solution $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{H}(r^{*})$.
item.dc:creator: Anvarbek Meirmanov, Akbota Senkebayeva

item.title: Dynamics of the Density Cube
item.description: arXiv:2606.02421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Density cube theory extends the canonical quantum density matrix $\rho_{ij}$ with the addition of an extra index to $\rho_{ijk}$. The elements of the density cube with two different indices, $\rho_{iij}$ and $\rho_{ijj}$, correspond to the real and imaginary parts of the off-diagonal element $\rho_{ij}$ of the density matrix and describe double-path interference, while those with three different indices describe non-canonical triple-path interference. In this letter, we propose an equation of motion for the density cube, obtained from the quantization of ternary Nambu dynamics, and find that pairs of triple-path interferences oscillate into each other.
item.dc:creator: Nabin Bhatta, Djordje Minic, Tatsu Takeuchi

item.title: The contrast between real and $p$-adic integrability
item.description: arXiv:2606.24363v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A fundamental question in $p$-adic symplectic geometry and $p$-adic Hamiltonian mechanics is to what extent we can learn new information about integrable systems with coefficients in the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, if we view them as $p$-adic systems instead of real ones. We combine geometric analytic estimates with Galois theory in order to show that at a local level, these real and $p$-adic viewpoints give completely different information. Then we focus on understanding this local behavior for the $p$-adic case by proving effective methods to compute local normal forms. Our results are motivated by a program outlined by Pelayo-Voevodsky-Warren a decade ago, to develop a $p$-adic theory of integrable systems and symplectic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Luis Crespo, \'Alvaro Pelayo

item.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
item.description: arXiv:2608.24164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. The final model attains a validation precision of 0.919, recall of 0.905, and $F_1$ of 0.912, and yields 29,605 dual-nucleus candidates after removing star-dominated and blended detections. Structured visual inspection indicates that $54.5$--$62\%$ are consistent with genuine dual nuclei, implying $\sim(1.4$--$1.8)\times10^{4}$ plausible systems. Cross-calibrating the YOLO separation against the deterministic GOTHIC centroid measurement and restricting to the compact regime ($d \le 6.87''$) gives a conservative subset of $\sim 13{,}672$ candidates, reaching calibrated separations of $\sim 0.56''$. Spectroscopy of the most compact ($\le 1$ kpc) systems shows spectra dominated by stellar absorption, with no resolved double-peaked emission, so confirmation requires higher-resolution follow-up. The catalogue is a statistically refined list of candidates, not confirmed DAGN. Nonetheless, deep-learning detection substantially reduces contamination and expands the plausible DAGN census.
item.dc:creator: Bhavesh Mukheja, Snehanshu Saha, Anwesh Bhattacharya, Mousumi Das, Fran\c{c}oise Combes, Sudhanshu Barway

item.title: Field-Modified Quantum Potentials from Tridiagonal Representations: Analytical Spectra and Galerkin Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2609.23348v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an effective radial framework for analyzing new field-modified potential function of a charged spinless particle in collinear electric and magnetic fields. Using the weak- magnetic field approximation, we neglect the diamagnetic term and other angular projections under an explicit smallness condition $\ll \Delta E$, where $E$ is the electric field, and the replacement of the angular factor by $C=\cos\theta$ in the spherical coordinates. The resulting equation is therefore a field-aligned radial model whose validity is limited to angularly localized states. Within this setting, we apply the indirect mode (or search mode) of Tridiagonal representation approach in the Laguerre and Jacobi bases. In the Laguerre basis, the tridiagonal constraint generates linear-plus-inverse and linear-plus-quadratic radial potentials, and the coefficient recurrences are connected with Meixner--Pollaczek and Meixner polynomial type structures, therefore yielding the analytic spectra and expansion wavefunctions. In the Jacobi basis, the mapping of the radial half-line to a finite interval produces a singular confining effective potential and a three-term recurrence that is treated through a truncated generalized eigenvalue problem. The formulation provides analytically and numerically tractable benchmark models for field-modified potential functions, while keeping the assumptions, parameter restrictions, endpoint behavior, and convergence tests explicit. In the Laguerre basis the resultant spectra are obtained in closed form and are independent of the orientation and of the electric field, which enter through the shape of the effective central potential, whereas in the Jacobi basis the spectrum is obtained numerically from a new three-term recurrence; in all cases the magnetic field enters through a linear Zeeman shift.
item.dc:creator: Tunde Joseph Osunmusanmi, Berihu Teklu

item.title: The Fixed-$q$ Edge Limit of the $q$-Krawtchouk Ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2609.24149v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the fixed-$q$ right-edge asymptotics of the ordinary $q$-Krawtchouk ensemble. For $0<q<1$, finite polynomial duality gives a direct proof of convergence of the correlation kernels to an explicit limiting kernel. The local Jacobi limit is a shifted continuous $q^{-1}$-Hermite expression with an indeterminate moment problem, so the limiting Jacobi expression does not determine a unique self-adjoint operator. A single spectral atom, asymptotically saturating the mass bound, selects the realization and yields strong-resolvent convergence. The limiting kernel represents its positive spectral projection and admits spectral-series, Christoffel--Darboux, and partial-theta representations. After a ground-state transformation, the associated dual operator agrees with a two-step spatial Markov operator of Borodin--Corwin. For $q>1$, the limiting Jacobi operator is of Al-Salam--Carlitz~I type and is essentially self-adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Nikitin

item.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.18081v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative
item.dc:creator: Nur Valeev

item.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
item.description: arXiv:2610.27263v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.
item.dc:creator: Andre M. Sonnet, Epifanio G. Virga

item.title: The degree distribution in bipartite planar maps: applications to the Ising model
item.description: arXiv:math/0211070v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize the generating function of bipartite planar maps counted according to the degree distribution of their black and white vertices. This result is applied to the solution of the hard particle and Ising models on random planar lattices. We thus recover and extend some results previously obtained by means of matrix integrals. Proofs are purely combinatorial and rely on the idea that planar maps are conjugacy classes of trees. In particular, these trees explain why the solutions of the Ising and hard particle models on maps of bounded degree are always algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Mireille Bousquet-M\'elou, Gilles Schaeffer
